sourceBindings.text: What two demonstrations really show
A crisp carrot is compared with a limp one; a cut celery petiole stands in tinted water for several hours.
The carrot contrast illustrates cell water pressure and firmness, not a field diagnosis by itself.
Color appearing higher in celery reveals a pathway for water movement through vascular tissue; record elapsed time and observation.
The dye is not a measurement of fertiliser uptake, and plant transpiration is different from water evaporating directly from soil.
Explain turgor and water transport, then state each demonstration's limit.

sourceBindings.text: Order a soil profile after wetting
A soil is initially saturated, then drains and later dries as roots extract water.
At saturation pores are water-filled; excess gravity water can move downward if drainage permits.
After drainable water leaves, field capacity is the upper reference for stored plant-available water.
As soil dries toward permanent wilting point, the available portion shrinks; AWC is FC − PWP.
Saturation → field capacity → permanent wilting point as drying proceeds, with a downward drainage arrow above FC and an AWC bracket between FC and PWP.

sourceBindings.text: Subtract on a common basis
A labelled practice layer has field capacity 30% by volume and permanent wilting point 12% by volume.
Both values use the same basis and layer.
30 − 12 = 18 percentage points by volume.
Without layer thickness, rooting pattern, crop demand and irrigation efficiency, this is not a field watering dose.
AWC = 18 percentage points by volume for the given example layer.

sourceBindings.text: Texture is one clue, not a schedule
Two fields are called sandy and clay-rich. Someone proposes fixed daily versus weekly irrigation solely from those names.
Sands often drain faster and may have lower per-depth AWC; clays can retain more total water, with a portion held too tightly.
Compare actual root-zone depth, structure, salinity, stage, evapotranspiration and irrigation capacity.
Check moisture or a suitable sensor and the crop's condition before setting interval and amount.
A tendency may guide a measurement plan, but neither schedule follows from texture alone.
